name: Oats Pancakes
steps: Whisk the oat flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl. In a separate bowl whisk the milk, curd and vanilla until smooth, then pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and fold just until no flour pockets remain.

Leave the batter for 10 minutes so the oat flour absorbs moisture. It should be thick but drop from a spoon; if it becomes stiff, mix in a small splash of water. Avoid beating it after the rest or the pancakes may become heavy.

Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned griddle over medium-low heat. Brush with a little of the measured oil and pour about one-eighth of the batter for each pancake, leaving room for it to spread into a small round.

Cook for 2–3 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges look set. Turn gently and cook for another 1–2 minutes until the centre springs back and there is no wet batter. Repeat with the remaining batter and oil, lowering the heat if the surface darkens too quickly.
Stack two warm pancakes per person. Divide the washed berries over the four plates and drizzle the measured maple syrup evenly over them. Serve promptly while the pancakes are fluffy.
tips: Oat flour absorbs liquid as it rests, so judge batter thickness just before cooking. Use fresh baking powder for a light texture.
passiveTime: Rest the batter for 10 minutes so the oat flour hydrates.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
